about.message: Abigail’s Driving School was started in 2012 by two Virginia Commonwealth University students. After both received traffic infractions, they had to attend a court mandated driver improvement class. During this class, they noticed Spanish speakers had to get an interpreter, which meant they would pay for the interpreter in addition to the class. The students were inspired to create a driving school which was able to provide classes in Spanish and English at a reasonable price. As a result, Abigail's Driving School became the first English-and-Spanish-language driving school provider in the Richmond Metropolitan area. Not only do we strive to overcome language barriers but also work hard to deliver the highest quality of customer service. We teach individuals defensive driving, regardless of age or experience. This consists of decreasing anxiety through practice, reinforcement and achieving customized goals. Our instructors have successfully passed an in-depth driving/criminal history check, are certified and licensed to teach by the Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles. Abigail’s Driving School is authorized, bonded, insured and certified by the Department of Motor Vehicles of Virginia. Vision: To become a household name in Virginia by ensuring each student can drive safely drive out on the streets and the in real world while facing different variable and dangers from their surrounding environment. Mission: To provide a learning friendly environment that consists of decreasing anxiety through practice, reinforcement and achieving customized goals.

course.description: The driver improvement clinic educates and refreshes both new and experienced drivers about defensive driving techniques in order to minimize risk. We are State of Virginia DMV Approved and Licensed. Program: Our driver improvement course uses the National Traffic Safety Institute (NTSI) Defensive Driving Program. NTSI is one of the first defensive driving programs established in 1974. Abigail's Driving School follows NTSI's belief that values + attitude = behavior. It is through personal responsibility that has the potential to modify driving behaviors.

va_license_1820.both_text_1: The 2027 requirement applies to applicants who are 18, 19, or 20 years old and have never held a driver's license from Virginia, another state, a U.S. territory, or a foreign country. If you previously held a license, this new requirement may not apply to you — but a learner's permit from another state is not a previous license, and it does not exempt you.
va_license_1820.both_text_2: For everyone the rule covers, the two pieces work together. You hold your permit while you complete driver education: finishing the course does not erase the 90-day permit period, and reaching day 90 does not excuse you from the course. Plan on both from the start.
va_license_1820.changes_intro: House Bill 1224 (2026 Acts of Assembly, Chapter 754; identical to Senate Bill 396) amended § 46.2-324.1 of the Code of Virginia. The change is narrow: it adds a combined requirement for first-time applicants ages 18 to 20 and leaves every other age group as it is today.
va_license_1820.changes_title: What changes in 2027 — and what stays the same
va_license_1820.cta_text: Every week spent deciding is a week added to your earliest license date. Book the complete adult package today — classroom online plus behind-the-wheel — and we will review your eligibility and testing arrangements before you start.
va_license_1820.cta_title: The 90-day clock starts with your permit
va_license_1820.faq_1_a: First-time applicants ages 18, 19, and 20 must meet two requirements together: complete a state-approved driver education program and hold a Virginia learner's permit for at least 90 days. The rule comes from House Bill 1224, which amended § 46.2-324.1 of the Code of Virginia.
va_license_1820.faq_2_a: For a license issued on or after January 1, 2027, at least 90 days — and completing driver education is also required. For licenses issued through December 31, 2026, the older choice applies: 60 days on a permit plus the DMV road skills test, or driver education instead.
va_license_1820.faq_2_q: How long do I have to hold a learner's permit if I am 19?
va_license_1820.faq_3_a: No. The permit period and driver education are separate requirements for first-time applicants ages 18 to 20, and one does not substitute for the other.
va_license_1820.faq_3_q: Can holding my permit for 90 days replace driver education?
va_license_1820.faq_4_a: Thirty-six classroom sessions, seven driving sessions, and seven observation sessions — each 50 minutes — plus a final road skills examination taken through the program. The school then submits your completion certificate to DMV.
va_license_1820.faq_4_q: What does a state-approved driver education program include?
va_license_1820.faq_5_a: Yes. If your license is issued after January 1, 2027, you must show proof of completed driver education even if your learner's permit was issued before that date.
va_license_1820.faq_5_q: I got my permit in 2026, but my license will be issued in 2027. Does the new rule apply to me?
va_license_1820.faq_6_a: If you can show you previously held a driver's license from another state, a U.S. territory, or a foreign country, the new requirement may not apply to you. A learner's permit from another state does not count as a previous license.
va_license_1820.faq_6_q: What if I had a license or permit in another state?
va_license_1820.faq_7_a: Nothing. First-time applicants age 21 and older keep the existing choice: hold a permit for at least 60 days, or complete an approved driver education program.
va_license_1820.faq_7_q: I am 21 or older. What changes for me in 2027?
va_license_1820.faq_8_a: Yes. Approved schools may offer the classroom portion online. The driving and observation sessions and the final road skills examination are completed in person with the school.
va_license_1820.faq_8_q: Can I take the classroom portion online?
va_license_1820.intro: Virginia is changing how first-time drivers ages 18 to 20 get licensed. If you have never held a driver's license and plan to apply in 2027, two requirements will apply to you at the same time — and one of them is a fixed 90-day wait that no class can shorten. This guide explains the new rule, who it covers, and how to plan your timeline here in Richmond.
va_license_1820.mistake_1_text: It does not. For first-time applicants ages 18 to 20, the permit period and the driver education program are separate requirements, and both must be met.
va_license_1820.mistake_1_title: Assuming the 90 days replaces driver education
va_license_1820.mistake_2_text: The 90-day permit period is a fixed wait that starts only when DMV issues your permit. If you need a license for a job, school, or a move, count backward from that date and start early.
va_license_1820.mistake_2_title: Waiting until the license is urgent
va_license_1820.mistake_3_text: Holding a learner's permit from another state does not make you a previously licensed driver. Only proof of a prior license may exempt you from the new requirement.
va_license_1820.mistake_3_title: Counting an out-of-state permit as a previous license
va_license_1820.mistake_4_text: Private lessons and a state-approved driver education program are different products. Before you pay, confirm the school is DMV-licensed to provide the complete program: classroom, driving, observation, and the final road skills exam.
va_license_1820.mistake_4_title: Choosing a school that is not licensed for the full program
va_license_1820.option_1_text: The complete package: the online classroom program plus the behind-the-wheel driving and observation program — the full driver education program the 2027 rule requires, in one enrollment.
va_license_1820.option_2_text: The classroom portion online, at your own pace: $200 tuition plus $7 processing. Behind-the-wheel training is completed separately.
va_license_1820.option_3_text: Already finished an approved classroom program? Complete the driving and observation sessions and the final road skills examination with our instructors.
va_license_1820.options_intro: Abigail's Driving School is a DMV-licensed driving school in Richmond, Virginia, with instruction and support in English and Spanish. Here is how our programs line up with the new requirement:
va_license_1820.program_1: 36 classroom sessions of 50 minutes each — the classroom portion may be completed online with an approved school
va_license_1820.program_2: 7 driving sessions of 50 minutes behind the wheel with a licensed instructor
va_license_1820.program_3: 7 observation sessions of 50 minutes watching another student drive
va_license_1820.program_4: A final road skills examination, taken through the program rather than at a DMV office
va_license_1820.program_intro: A state-approved driver education program is a complete program, not a handful of private lessons. Virginia's standard program includes:
va_license_1820.program_outro: When you finish, the driver training school sends your completion certificate to DMV. DMV does not accept completion certificates handed in by applicants, so choose a school that is licensed to run the full program and submit your record.
va_license_1820.program_title: What counts as driver education in Virginia
va_license_1820.row_adult_after: Both are required: complete an approved driver education program while holding your permit, and hold the permit for at least 90 days.
va_license_1820.row_adult_before: Your choice: complete an approved driver education program, or hold a permit at least 60 days and pass the DMV road skills test.
va_license_1820.row_older_after: No change — the same choice continues.
va_license_1820.row_older_before: Your choice: hold a permit at least 60 days, or complete an approved driver education program.
va_license_1820.row_teen_after: No change — the same requirements continue.
va_license_1820.row_teen_before: Approved driver education, permit held at least 9 months, and 45 hours of supervised driving (15 after sunset) certified by a parent or guardian.
va_license_1820.seo_description: From January 1, 2027, first-time Virginia applicants ages 18–20 must complete driver education AND hold a learner's permit for 90 days. A Richmond guide from Abigail's Driving School: the new rules, a step-by-step timeline, FAQs, and the $549 adult package.
va_license_1820.seo_title: Virginia Driver's License at 18–20: New 2027 Rules (HB 1224)
va_license_1820.sources: Sources: Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles (driver education and driver's license eligibility information) and Code of Virginia § 46.2-324.1, as amended by House Bill 1224, 2026 Acts of Assembly, Chapter 754.
va_license_1820.step_1: Study the Virginia Driver's Manual and prepare for the two-part knowledge exam.
va_license_1820.step_2: Pass the knowledge exam and receive your learner's permit. Your 90-day clock starts on the day the permit is issued.
va_license_1820.step_3: Enroll in a state-approved driver education program. You can start the classroom portion online right away.
va_license_1820.step_5: Practice driving with a licensed driver throughout the 90-day permit period — do not leave all of your driving for the formal sessions.
va_license_1820.step_6: Complete the 7 driving sessions and 7 observation sessions with your school.
va_license_1820.step_7: Pass the final road skills examination through the program.
va_license_1820.step_8: Your school submits your completion certificate to DMV.
va_license_1820.step_9: Finish the remaining DMV licensing steps and receive your driver's license.
va_license_1820.summary_1: Starting January 1, 2027, first-time applicants who are 18, 19, or 20 must complete a state-approved driver education program and hold a Virginia learner's permit for at least 90 days. Both are required — one does not replace the other.
va_license_1820.summary_2: What matters is the date your license is issued. A license issued after January 1, 2027 requires proof of driver education, even if you received your learner's permit in 2026.
va_license_1820.summary_3: Getting licensed on or before December 31, 2026? The current rules still apply: complete approved driver education, or hold your permit at least 60 days and pass the DMV road skills test.
va_license_1820.summary_4: Age 21 or older: nothing changes in 2027. The choice between a 60-day permit period and driver education continues.

faq_page.help_text: Tell us what you need to complete, and we will help you check the course, the format, and the next steps before you register or book.
faq_page.help_title: Still unsure which course you need?
faq_page.intro: Quick answers about getting a Virginia driver's license, our courses and prices, booking lessons, online courses, and classes in Spanish. If your question is not answered here, call us at (804) 256-3147 — press 2 for Spanish.
faq_page.q10_a: Lessons and the behind-the-wheel program are booked online through our Setmore booking page: pick the service, the instructor, and a time that works for you. Booking a multi-session program? Please choose all of your session times up front. Online courses work differently — enroll through the course links on this website, then complete the course on the course platform.
faq_page.q10_q: How do I book a lesson or a class?
faq_page.q11_a: Please cancel or reschedule at least 24 hours before your appointment's start time. You can manage an appointment through Setmore; if something comes up inside 24 hours, contact the school directly. The full policy is on our booking policy page.
faq_page.q12_a: We offer in-car lessons and behind-the-wheel sessions on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Fridays, plus alternating weekends. We do not teach on Wednesdays or Thursdays. When you book, the calendar shows the times currently open.
faq_page.q13_a: We teach in the Richmond, Virginia area, and in-person classes are held in Richmond. Pickup for lessons is arranged at booking time, so tell us where to meet you when you reserve. Online courses are available to eligible students anywhere in Virginia.
faq_page.q14_a: Enroll and pay through the course links on this website, then complete the course on the course platform at your own pace during your access period. When you finish, your completion is reported or certificated the way DMV requires for that course. For driver education programs, the school submits the completion certificate to DMV — DMV does not accept certificates from applicants, so please do not mail yours in.
faq_page.q14_q: How do the online courses work?
faq_page.q15_a: Yes. Instructor Ileana Romero teaches in-person classes in Spanish: Driver's Manual for $250, Driver Improvement for $100, and RADEP for $200. For the re-examination class, there is an extra benefit: if you failed the DMV written test three times, when you complete the class you receive your certificate from us — issued right here, in Spanish, which not every school does. To reserve a Spanish class, call or text her directly at (703) 637-8250. You can also reach us on the main line, (804) 256-3147 — press 2 for Spanish.
faq_page.q15_q: Do you offer classes in Spanish?
faq_page.q1_a: It depends on your age. Under 18, you must complete a state-approved driver education program, hold your learner's permit for at least nine months, and log 45 hours of supervised driving — including 15 hours after sunset — certified by a parent or guardian. At 18 and older, you start with a learner's permit, and you qualify either through driver education or a permit-holding period; the exact rules differ for ages 18–20 and 21+, and they change on January 1, 2027. Our guide walks through each age group step by step.
faq_page.q1_q: What do I need to get a Virginia driver's license for the first time?
faq_page.q2_a: Under House Bill 1224, a first-time applicant who is 18, 19, or 20 and has never held a license must do both of two things before a license can be issued on or after January 1, 2027: complete a state-approved driver education program and hold a Virginia learner's permit for at least 90 days. One does not replace the other. Applicants 21 and older keep the current choice: hold the permit for 60 days or complete driver education. If your license will be issued after January 1, 2027, the new rule applies to you even if you received your permit in 2026.
faq_page.q2_q: What changes on January 1, 2027 for ages 18 to 20?
faq_page.q3_a: Virginia requires you to complete the classroom component of driver education — the Driver's Manual re-examination course — before you can take the knowledge exam a fourth time. We offer that course online for $154.22 total. If you prefer a classroom setting, we also run in-person re-exam classes in English and Spanish: $175 on weekdays and $250 on weekends. When you complete the course with us, we issue your certificate of completion — the document DMV requires before your fourth attempt.
faq_page.q3_q: I failed the DMV knowledge exam three times. What do I have to do now?
faq_page.q4_a: The online Driver Improvement course is $98.33 total. It is an 8-hour course from a DMV-licensed school, and it can be used to satisfy Virginia court orders and DMV requirements. Prefer to sit in a classroom? In-person Driver Improvement in Spanish with our instructor costs $100.
faq_page.q4_q: How much is the online Driver Improvement course?
faq_page.q5_a: That is the court's decision, not ours. A court can order you to complete Driver Improvement and can take your completion into account, but no driving school can promise that a ticket will be dismissed, a charge reduced, or points removed. Separately, DMV can award safe-driving points for completing the course under its own rules. Show us your court order or DMV notice before you enroll, and we will confirm the course matches your requirement.
faq_page.q5_q: Will Driver Improvement dismiss my ticket or take points off my record?
faq_page.q6_a: RADEP — the Reckless/Aggressive Driving Education Program — is an education program ordered by a court or DMV for certain reckless or aggressive driving offenses. Online, the 4-hour course is $93.15 total and the 12-hour program is $186.30 total. In-person RADEP in Spanish with our instructor Ileana costs $200. Your court order will say whether you need the 4-hour or the 12-hour program — check it before enrolling.
faq_page.q6_q: What is RADEP, and what does it cost?
faq_page.q7_a: The behind-the-wheel program is $425. In its standard format you complete seven 50-minute driving sessions and seven 50-minute observation sessions, paired with another student, and you finish with the final road skills examination. If no second student is available to pair with you, the program is delivered instead as seven 1-hour one-on-one sessions. The program is classroom-first: the online classroom component comes before your in-car sessions.
faq_page.q7_q: What does the behind-the-wheel program include, and how much does it cost?
faq_page.q8_a: A private lesson is $80 for 60 minutes of one-on-one instruction. If you plan to practice regularly, a package of five 60-minute lessons is $375. Lessons are booked online, and your pickup point is arranged when you book.
faq_page.q8_q: How much are private driving lessons?
faq_page.q9_a: Yes — the Adult Online Classroom + Behind-the-Wheel Package is $549. It combines the online classroom driver education course with the complete behind-the-wheel program, so adult students get the full driver education program in one enrollment. It is also the complete program first-time applicants ages 18 to 20 will need under the January 1, 2027 rule.
faq_page.q9_q: Is there a package for adults that combines classroom and behind-the-wheel?
